name: es30-depth-textures
title: Depth Textures
summary: All five ES 3.0 depth formats (DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24/32F, DEPTH24_STENCIL8, DEPTH32F_STENCIL8) as textures: Table 3.2 uploads read back bit-exactly or within one step of the stored precision, nine invalid format/type combinations rejected; a 3D scene and gl_FragDepth strips rendered into every format and checked against the §2.1.6 / §3.9.2.3 conversion rules and a CPU ray caster; the eight compare functions through sampler2DShadow, sampler2DArrayShadow and samplerCubeShadow (Dref clamped only for fixed-point formats); LINEAR comparisons (all-pass 1, all-fail 0); depth-texture completeness and GenerateMipmap errors; the stencil half of the depth-stencil formats uploaded, cleared, written and read back through the stencil test.
spec: ES 3.0 §2.1.6.1 / §2.1.6.2 Fixed-Point Data Conversions (eq. 2.1, 2.3: one of the two nearest b-bit values)
ES 3.0 §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (fixed-point window z k / (2^m - 1))

ES 3.0 §3.7.2 Transfer of Pixel Rectangles (Table 3.2 valid format/type/internalformat combinations, Tables 3.8 / 3.9 UNSIGNED_INT_24_8 and FLOAT_32_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8_REV, §3.7.2.2 component count mismatch, §3.7.2.3 conversion to floating point)

ES 3.0 §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification (depth clamped to [0, 1]; depth formats only for TEXTURE_2D, TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY, TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP; Table 3.14 depth and stencil resolutions; §3.8.3.1 required formats), §3.8.5 TexSubImage constraints
ES 3.0 §3.8.10.5 Manual Mipmap Generation (INVALID_OPERATION unless color-renderable and texture-filterable)
ES 3.0 §3.8.12 Combined Depth/Stencil Textures (the stencil component is ignored by texturing)
ES 3.0 §3.8.13 Texture Completeness (sized depth format with compare mode NONE needs mag NEAREST and min NEAREST or NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST), §3.8.13.1 sampler objects
ES 3.0 §3.8.15.1 Depth Texture Comparison Mode (Table 3.23, clamping of Dt / Dref for fixed-point formats only, filtered comparisons implementation-dependent)

ES 3.0 §3.9.2.1 Texture Access (Cb = (Rt, 0, 0, 1); incomplete texture returns (0, 0, 0, 1) or 0 for a shadow sampler), §3.9.2.3 Shader Outputs (gl_FragDepth clamp and conversion), Table 3.21 cube map face selection
ES 3.0 §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test (no depth write when disabled), §4.1.4 Stencil Test, §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (ClearBufferfv DEPTH, ClearBufferfi)
ES 3.0 §4.4.2 Attaching Images to Framebuffer Objects (DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT, FramebufferTextureLayer), §4.4.4.1 Framebuffer Attachment Completeness
ES 3.0 §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries (DEPTH_SIZE, STENCIL_SIZE, COMPONENT_TYPE; INVALID_OPERATION for COMPONENT_TYPE of DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT and for different depth / stencil objects)

GLSL ES 3.00 §4.1.7 Samplers, §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers (shadow and array samplers have none), §7.2 gl_FragDepth / gl_FragCoord, §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions (shadow forms: Dref = last component, array layer = second to last)

api.glGenTextures: scene, array, cube, strip, upload, probe and scratch textures, all observed through validated lookups
api.glBindTexture: TEXTURE_2D, TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY, TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP and TEXTURE_3D bindings; the same depth texture on a raw and a comparing unit returns depth and comparison results respectively
api.glActiveTexture: six units with six sampler types (raw / shadow 2D, array, cube); per-unit results differ as expected
api.glTexImage2D: DEPTH_COMPONENT16 (UNSIGNED_SHORT and UNSIGNED_INT), DEPTH_COMPONENT24 (UNSIGNED_INT), DEPTH_COMPONENT32F (FLOAT, -0.25 / 1.75 clamped), DEPTH24_STENCIL8 (UNSIGNED_INT_24_8) and DEPTH32F_STENCIL8 (FLOAT_32_UNSIGNED_INT_24_8_REV) read back per texel, stencil read back through the stencil test; cube faces; INVALID_OPERATION for nine invalid combinations
api.glTexImage3D: DEPTH_COMPONENT32F 2D array upload read back per layer; INVALID_OPERATION for a depth format on TEXTURE_3D, NO_ERROR on TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY
api.glTexSubImage2D: UNSIGNED_INT data into DEPTH_COMPONENT16 accepted and sampled back; UNSIGNED_SHORT into DEPTH_COMPONENT24 rejected with INVALID_OPERATION and the texel unchanged; FLOAT / UNSIGNED_INT fills of immutable textures
api.glTexStorage2D: immutable DEPTH formats (scene, strips, cube) whose stored values are read back; single-level storage keeps NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST complete
api.glTexStorage3D: DEPTH_COMPONENT32F 2-layer array rendered per layer and read back against the CPU model
api.glTexParameteri: MIN/MAG filters decide completeness (§3.8.13) and NEAREST vs LINEAR comparisons; COMPARE_MODE / COMPARE_FUNC switch the shadow results exactly as Table 3.23 predicts (Dref clamping for 24-bit fixed-point formats strict, ANGLE XFAIL) (typed glTexParameter overloads)
api.glGetTexParameteriv: initial COMPARE_MODE NONE / COMPARE_FUNC LEQUAL; each of the eight functions reads back
api.glGenerateMipmap: INVALID_OPERATION on all five depth formats and on a level-0-only DEPTH_COMPONENT32F that stays mipmap-incomplete afterwards; NO_ERROR on RGBA8
api.glGenSamplers: raw NEAREST/NONE sampler, LINEAR display sampler and eight comparing samplers, all observed through lookups
api.glSamplerParameteri: COMPARE_MODE / COMPARE_FUNC of the sampler supersede the texture's (2D array lookups follow Table 3.23 while the texture's compare mode is NONE); NEAREST filters; read back
api.glGetSamplerParameteriv: COMPARE_REF_TO_TEXTURE and the function of each of the eight comparing samplers
api.glBindSampler: raw and comparing sampler objects on two units reading the same texture (window grid band and upper part)
api.glGenFramebuffers: depth-only, depth-stencil, layer, cube-face, strip, probe and stencil read-out framebuffers, each producing validated output
api.glBindFramebuffer: render-to-depth targets, the probe target and the default framebuffer
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: DEPTH_ATTACHMENT, DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT (texture named at DEPTH and STENCIL), STENCIL_ATTACHMENT alone, cube faces; depth texture at COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 / STENCIL_ATTACHMENT gives FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT
api.glFramebufferTextureLayer: both layers of the DEPTH_COMPONENT32F array rendered from two cameras and checked against the CPU ray caster
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE for every depth format and for DEPTH24_STENCIL8 alone at STENCIL_ATTACHMENT; INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT for a depth-only format at STENCIL / COLOR_ATTACHMENT0
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: DEPTH_SIZE >= Table 3.14, STENCIL_SIZE >= 8, COMPONENT_TYPE UNSIGNED_NORMALIZED / FLOAT, OBJECT_TYPE / OBJECT_NAME; INVALID_OPERATION for COMPONENT_TYPE of DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT and when depth and stencil objects differ
api.glClearBufferfv: DEPTH clear value 0.8125 stored per the conversion rules (strip texel 15) and 1.0 read back exactly in sky texels
api.glClearBufferfi: depth 0.8125 and stencil 0xA5 of both depth-stencil formats read back (sampling and stencil test)
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST (needed for depth writes, LESS keeps the nearest surface, LESS against the texture's depth in the stencil test) and STENCIL_TEST
api.glDepthFunc: LESS (scene depth equals the nearest CPU hit; strip depth-fail/depth-pass decides the stencil op), ALWAYS (every gl_FragDepth value written)
api.glStencilFunc: ALWAYS with the object id (scene stencil = id of the visible object) and EQUAL with ref = mask = 1 << bit (bit-wise stencil read-out)
api.glStencilOp: KEEP/KEEP/REPLACE writes object ids; KEEP/INCR/REPLACE gives 0x3C on depth pass and 0xA6 on depth fail exactly as predicted
api.glColorMask: one channel per stencil bit in the read-out passes; the eight bits of every texel are recovered exactly
api.glUniform1fv: gl_FragDepth values per strip texel and the probe references, observed in the stored depth and the comparison results
api.glUniform4fv: probe coordinates (texel centers, array layers, cube directions) select the expected texels
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: camera, second camera and six cube-face view-projections: stored depths match the CPU ray caster
api.glDrawArrays: scene meshes, gl_VertexID full-screen passes for strips, probes, stencil read-out, panels and grid cells; all outputs validated
api.glViewport: 15x1 strip viewport leaves texel 15 at its clear value; panel and grid cell viewports at every window size
api.glReadPixels: RGBA_INTEGER / UNSIGNED_INT read-back of the RGBA32UI probe target (bit-exact floats) and RGBA8 read-back of the window and the stencil passes

visual_review.notes: Viewed the 256x256 ctest captures of gpu (radeonsi) and zink es-max plus 800x800, 333x777 and 1280x400 radeonsi captures. Top: five cover-fitted depth-texture panels (3 + 2 rows at square sizes, 2 + 2 + 1 in portrait, one row of 5 at 1280x400) of the same scene: violet sky, pink-to-violet ground with unit-distance contour stripes, relief-shaded boxes; the DEPTH_COMPONENT16 panel shows speckled stair-step shading on the far purple and teal boxes, 24/32F are smooth; the two depth-stencil panels tint the boxes green/blue/orange/red/violet/cyan from the stencil ids. Bottom: 8 x 3 compare grid with per-function colors; the bottom band is bright for EQUAL, LEQUAL, GEQUAL, ALWAYS and dark for the others; LEQUAL and GREATER cells are visibly complementary silhouettes; NEVER is dark, ALWAYS lit with depth shading; the cube row shows the panorama around the cube center. The window is filled at every size without stretching.
